title: VPC IaC deploy safety orchestrator: Conftest/OPA gates + canary upgrades + runtime health probes
creator: Ariana Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a safe, auditable CI/CD orchestrator for Terraform-based VPC/private deployments that enforces policy-as-code (Conftest/OPA), produces gated plan artifacts, performs staged (canary) upgrades, and validates runtime health via automated probes before promoting changes to production.

Background: Private deployments require stricter controls for network and infra changes. Current pipelines run terraform plan/apply but lack an integrated policy scoring system, an automated canary promotion flow, and runtime verification post-apply. This leads to manual rollbacks and slower upgrades.

Scope:
- Create a reusable pipeline job (ci/terraform/vpc-deploy-orchestrator) that runs:
  1) fmt + validate + tflint
  2) terraform init + terraform plan (artifact stored with metadata: commit, module_version, module_checksum)
  3) Conftest (OPA) evaluation against the plan.json using curated policy bundle (policies/vpc/*.rego) producing a policy score and a violation report (JSON + human-readable summary)
  4) Policy gate evaluation: policies with severity=deny block the pipeline; warnings increase a score but do not block if below threshold. Default gate: deny violations => fail; warning score >= 50 => block (configurable per project).
  5) If plan + policy pass, create a canary workspace apply against a customer-isolated canary VPC (tagged:canary) with a short TTL (72h)
  6) Post-apply runtime probes: automated health checks that exercise control plane endpoints, network connectivity, and RBAC access. Probes run via k6 + curl + small smoke tasks and report metrics to the console dashboard.
  7) Canary monitoring window (default 2 hours) where health metrics, logs, and alert statuses are observed. If any critical probe fails or latency/error SLO breaches occur, auto-rollback: run terraform destroy in the canary workspace and mark plan as needing remediation.
  8) If canary passes, promote plan artifact to prod workspace and apply with a controlled concurrency window and an automatic small-batch rollout (configurable).

Acceptance criteria:
- Conftest runs against plan.json and produces both a structured JSON report and a score UI in Console.
- Policy gating is configurable per repo via .ci/policy-gate.yaml and enforced by the job.
- Canary apply + runtime probes are automated; passing probes are required before prod apply.
- All pipeline runs produce an immutable plan artifact with metadata and linkable to PR and ticket.
- Rollback path is documented and automated for canary failures.
- PagerDuty/Slack alerts for policy fails, canary probe failures, and apply errors are wired in.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Conftest (OPA) is selected for plan scanning because it operates on plan.json and is lightweight to integrate. We will bundle curated Rego policies owned by Security and Infra teams.
- Soft-gates vs hard-gates: enable a default hard block for security-relevant denies (public subnet additions, wide CIDR expansions, KMS disabled on secrets) while allowing teams to opt-in to stricter scoring thresholds for warnings. This reduces developer friction while enforcing critical rules.
- Artifact storage: use S3 bucket (private-deployments-terraform-plans) with lifecycle rules and indexing in the Console for auditability.
- Runtime probing must be opinionated but lightweight. Start with a defined base checklist: management endpoint ping, internal API auth smoke, outbound connectivity check, and a DB connection smoke (if applicable).

CI job names and example flow (for engineering to implement):
- jobs: { format-validate, tflint, terraform-plan-artifact, conftest-evaluate, policy-gate, terraform-apply-canary, runtime-probes, canary-monitor, promote-to-prod }
- Example GH Actions/Drone/GitLab steps and required secrets: TF_WORKSPACE, TF_VAR_customer_id, AWS_ROLE_ARN, POLICY_BUNDLE_S3_PATH, PAGERDUTY_KEY

Testing and rollout plan:
- Begin in a dedicated infra repo: infra/vpc-tests with a minimal module and test harness.
- Implement pipeline and run against a staging account.
- Run a controlled canary upgrade to inject a benign change; validate probes and rollback behavior.
- Gradual rollout: opt-in for 3 pilot customers, then enable as default for all internal infra repos after two successful cycles.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit events for: plan_created, policy_evaluated (score), canary_apply_started, canary_probe_failed, canary_promoted, canary_rolledback, prod_apply_started, prod_apply_failed.
- Surface policy scores and plan artifacts in Console on the PR and in ticket timeline.

Docs & artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821 (WIP)
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/INF/Policy+Gates+and+Canary+Orchestrator
- Policy bundle prototype: s3://policy-bundles/dev/vpc-bundle-2025-02-08.tar.gz

Open questions:
- What threshold should we use for warning-score block by default? (proposed 50)
- Should the canary workspace TTL be shorter (24h) for high-risk customers? (Ops input required)
